summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and gastroparesis was admitted after her mother found her unresponsive and hypothermic. She had experienced nausea and headache the prior day, ate only breakfast, and took her usual long-acting insulin, leading to severe hypoglycemia with a blood glucose of 25. She was treated with glucagon and IV dextrose, warmed with a bear hugger, and stabilized. She missed a dialysis session, contributing to fluid overload and hypertension, and underwent hemodialysis during admission. Her blood sugar fluctuated but stabilized on her home insulin regimen. Abdominal pain was attributed to chronic gastroparesis, and mild pulmonary congestion resolved. She improved clinically, regained mental clarity, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with instructions to continue her medications, attend dialysis, and follow up with her endocrinologist.
